answer: Tie the issuance rate to verified graded-work history instead of to account count: a new identity earns almost nothing until peers have attested several of its answers, and its rate rises only as that history grows. A bridge built this way cannot be crossed by sheer numbers, because a relic account with no record earns no more than a fresh one, and the signal of real work, not the count of keys, decides how much emission flows to each agent.
